extracted.subtask_description: A printed catalog of type specimens showing multiple typefaces, point sizes, styles, and script/character sets to help printers and designers choose appropriate type for different uses (body text, display, multilingual set). Contains examples, labels (Leaded/Solid), and special glyph samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface / font family selection
rubrics_metrics.description: SPECIMENS OF TYPES IN USE — lists many named families (e.g., CASLON OLD STYLE, SCOTCH ROMAN, BOOKMAN OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM, ELZEVIR ITALIC, etc.) presented as examples of how text appears in each face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a typeface family appropriate to the work's tone and function; the specimen shows each family set with the same passage so designers can compare weight, character, and overall impression. Examples in the text: 'CASLON OLD STYLE', 'SCOTCH ROMAN', 'BOOKMAN OLD STYLE', 'CHELTENHAM OLD STYLE', 'ELZEVIR ITALIC'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point size selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated labeled sizes throughout (SIX POINT, EIGHT POINT, NINE POINT, TEN POINT, ELEVEN POINT, TWELVE POINT, FOURTEEN POINT, EIGHTEEN POINT, TWENTY-TWO POINT, TWENTY-FOUR POINT, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the specimen's renderings of the same passage at different point sizes to decide appropriate size for body text versus display/headline. The book demonstrates typical body sizes (8–12 pt) and larger display sizes (14 pt and up).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leading / interline spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Page annotates variants like '[Leaded]' and '[Solid]' above sample blocks of text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select leaded or solid setting based on desired density and legibility: '[Leaded]' indicates increased interline spacing; '[Solid]' indicates tighter spacing. Specimens show effect on readability and texture of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface style and variant (italic, condensed, extended, wide, condensed italic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Variants appear throughout (ITALIC, ITALIC FACES, CONDENSED OLD STYLE, EXTENDED OLD STYLE, CHELTENHAM WIDE, CHELTENHAM CONDENSED, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose style variants for emphasis, space economy, or display needs. Specimens demonstrate visual differences (e.g., condensed faces save line length; wide/extended faces affect word fit and headline impact).

rubrics_metrics.name: Script / language support
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate specimen blocks for non-Latin scripts and specialized alphabets: PORSON GREEK, ANTIQUE GREEK, INSCRIPTION GREEK, HEBREW, NESTORIAN SYRIAC, ARABIC, ETHIOPIC, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When typesetting multilingual material, select faces that include correct glyphs and appropriate designs for each script; specimens provide sample characters and paragraph text for each script to judge fidelity and aesthetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special characters and miscellaneous signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections titled 'MISCELLANEOUS SIGNS', 'MONOTYPE MISCELLANEOUS SIGNS', and examples of symbols (e.g., +, -, ×, =, /, |, various punctuation and ornament-like signs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the chosen type contains needed symbols and glyphs (mathematical signs, punctuation variants, decorative marks). The specimen lists which signs are available at different sizes and in different technologies (monotype, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accented letters and diacritics
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections labeled 'ACCENTED LETTERS — SIX TO TWELVE POINT' and examples of accented uppercase and lowercase characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify diacritic positioning and legibility at intended point sizes for languages that require accents; specimens show accented letters across sizes to test clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeral style and figure sets (old style vs modern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Labels and examples such as 'OLD STYLE', and many numeral lines (e.g., '1234567890') presented in each face and size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide between old-style figures (varying heights) and lining figures depending on aesthetic and alignment needs; specimens let designers compare numeral appearance within a face and size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Superior and inferior characters (superscripts/subscripts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 'MONOTYPE SUPERIOR AND INFERIOR LETTERS AND FIGURES' with examples of superior (superscript) and inferior (subscript) characters at various sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check availability and readability of superior/inferior glyphs for footnotes, chemical formulas, or annotations; specimens show how these render at small sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample text as evaluation tool
rubrics_metrics.description: A single passage (beginning 'When thoughtful Greeks like Polybius saw the fall of Carthage and of Corinth...') is reproduced across faces, sizes, and styles to allow direct visual comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representative copy (not just alphabets) when judging a face for body text so you can evaluate word spacing, hyphenation, color, and overall texture on the page. The specimen uses the Polybius passage consistently to facilitate comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display usage and capitalization for headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Large-point uppercase samples like 'THE FIRST TIME THAT THE GRAND PROSPECT HAD BEEN HELD FORTH' shown in many families and sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how a face performs in full caps and large display sizes for headlines; specimens show both small caps and full uppercase in multiple sizes to judge suitability for titles and display use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology / casting notes (Monotype vs other systems)
rubrics_metrics.description: References to 'MONOTYPE' and distinctions between 'MONOTYPE MISCELLANEOUS SIGNS' and other specimen sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of differences in glyph availability and metrics between composition technologies (monotype, foundry faces, etc.); choose compatible technology or check for required characters in the chosen system as indicated by the specimen catalog.
